subject: Authorize automatic model failover for PearlCity - model-omega-4.2 latency regression
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@pearlcity.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@pearlcity.ai
Date: 2029-12-02T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Latency spike observed on model-omega-4.2 - immediate assistance needed

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing a sharp increase in generation p95 for the assistant endpoint using model-omega-4.2 around 07:45 PST. P95 jumped from ~380ms to ~1.6s and errors are rising (5xx rate ~0.6%). The spike correlates with a higher proportion of longer-context requests; we haven't changed our prompts or traffic patterns.

Can Redwood trigger an automatic failover to the prior stable variant (model-omega-4.1) while your team investigates? We need something to keep our SLAs intact — customers are calling.

Attached: pearlcity-p95-spike-20291202.csv (metrics excerpt)

Thanks,
Alice Turner
Head of Platform, PearlCity

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@pearlcity.ai>, Chris Lang <chris.lang@pearlcity.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-12-02T08:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike observed on model-omega-4.2 - immediate assistance needed

Alice — thanks for the heads-up and the CSV. We're seeing the same signal in platform telemetry. High-level plan proposed below; please confirm you'd like us to proceed with an automated fallback.

Proposed immediate actions (need customer approval to proceed):
- Activate automatic failover from model-omega-4.2 -> model-omega-4.1 for >=60% of traffic to the assistant endpoint.
- Enforce a 10-minute cooldown and circuit-breaker: if error rate >1% or p95 doesn't improve within 8 minutes, revert to 4.2 and open an incident.
- Open an engineering trace and capture KV cache/quantization metrics; attach logs and share follow-up within 60m.
- If accepted, we will also offer a one-time credit for impacted time window (Ben will confirm amount).

We need written OK from PearlCity to make the change. Ben / Markus / Monica: please stand by for execution. Markus, can you confirm the safe fallback path and estimated risk window?

— Soojin
Director, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference

On 2029-12-02 08:12, Alice Turner wrote:

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-12-02T08:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike observed on model-omega-4.2 - immediate assistance needed

Soojin / team — looking at recent deploy notes, model-omega-4.2 included a lightweight quantization pass to reduce mem footprint; initial hypothesis is KV-cache fragmentation under longer contexts combined with a kernel selection path that regresses on tail latency for certain sequence-length distributions.

Risk assessment for fallback to model-omega-4.1:
- Rollback path is safe: 4.1 uses the older kernel path and stable cache layout, no schema changes.
- Expected improvement: p95 should return to ~400-500ms based on canary replays.
- Known risk: slight throughput drop (~3-5%) under high concurrency due to less aggressive batching in 4.1; for PearlCity's traffic shape that should be acceptable compared to current degradation.

Execution steps (engineering):
1) Trigger traffic shift to model-omega-4.1 at the routing layer (can be manual or automated via circuit-breaker rules).
2) Start extended trace capture and a heap/kv-snapshot: omega42-trace-heapdump.txt (attached).
3) Monitor tokens/sec, p95, error rate; if metrics fail to improve, halt fallback and escalate to infra on-call.

I recommend we allow the automated failover with a 15-minute monitoring window and a manual sign-off if we need to re-roll forward. Give me 5m and I'll prepare the canary commands.

Attachments: omega42-trace-heapdump.txt (engineer trace)

On 2029-12-02 08:25, Soojin Lee wrote:

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Alice / team — PearlCity, you have our permission to execute the fallback we described. We will:
- Approve an immediate automatic failover to model-omega-4.1 for up to 75% traffic for 2x 10-minute cycles while we validate.
- Offer a service credit for any SLA gaps during the incident window; I'll follow up with an exact figure and get legal looped for the SLA exception amendment.

Monica — can you prepare the customer comms and a short DocuSign amendment for the temporary SLA carve-out? Including a one-line acceptance from PearlCity is sufficient to authorize the change.

— Ben
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

Alice — thanks. We have a short execution plan and a communication template below. If you reply "OK to proceed" we will start the controlled failover at 09:30 PST.

Customer-facing execution plan:
- 09:30 PST: Shift 60% traffic to model-omega-4.1 via routing policy; remaining 40% stays on 4.2 for comparison.
- 09:40 PST: Evaluate p95, error rate, and logs. If p95 improves by >=30% and errors drop, shift to 75% for another 10 minutes.
- 09:55 PST: If stable, keep 75% for 30 minutes then gradually return to normal routing and schedule a post-incident call.
- If any metric regresses, we will revert to 4.2 and open infra escalation.

Attachments and evidence paths:
- Crash/trace dump: omega42-trace-heapdump.txt
- Metrics: pearlcity-p95-spike-20291202.csv
- Post-incident notes: drive link https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/pc-post-incident-20291202

DocuSign amendment: https://docusign.com/external/pc-sla-exception-2029 (one-line acceptance from PearlCity required)

Please reply with exact wording you want in the customer acknowledgement if you prefer something other than "OK to proceed".

— Monica

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: 2029-12-04T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: PearlCity failover and telemetry findings

Alice / team — final update from our side. Following your approval on 2029-12-02 we executed the controlled failover at 09:30 PST and shifted 60% -> 75% to model-omega-4.1 over the next 25 minutes. Observations: 

- p95 improved from ~1.6s to ~420ms within 6 minutes of the initial shift.
- 5xx errors fell from 0.6% to 0.05%.
- Canary traces indicate high fragmentation in the omega-4.2 KV cache under long-context sessions; the quantization path triggered a slower kernel selection for specific attention lengths.

Next steps recommended:
1) Re-queue a targeted rollback test on a staging slice of 4.2 with modified quantization settings.
2) Schedule a joint RCA call with PearlCity and infra (I've proposed times in the shared calendar).
3) Ben will follow up with the agreed service credit and legal amendment confirmation.

Attachments: post-incident-notes-20291204.txt, omega42-trace-heapdump.txt

Thanks again for the fast coordination. If you'd like a quick debrief this afternoon, open a calendar invite and we'll join.

— Soojin
Director, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
